# Trajectory Planning and Action Chunking\chaptersubtitle{Diffusion Policies, Temporal Ensembling, and Jerk Continuity}

![**Systems Organ Focus:** Stage 5 (Trajectory Planning & Action Chunking). Acting as the System 1.5 proposal engine, the trajectory planner translates 1 Hz expiring intent leases from System 2 into continuous, multi-step action chunks ($H=16$), amortizing neural inference delay across physical time while guaranteeing $\mathcal{C}^2$ jerk continuity before passing candidate commands to the 1 kHz real-time MCU safety enforcer.](figures/fig_pipeline_locator.svg){#fig-locator-ch07 width=100% fig-pos="H"}

*Why does an AI policy that outputs smooth trajectories in simulation snap gear teeth and shake violently on a physical robot?*

In digital machine learning, sequential decision-making is framed as a Markov decision process where policies emit a single discrete action per time step. On physical hardware, this single-step paradigm breaks down: neural forward passes take tens of milliseconds, during which actuators are starved of fresh commands. When new actions finally arrive, discrete step changes command infinite acceleration derivatives, injecting violent mechanical jerk ($\dddot{\mathbf{q}} \to \infty$) that excites structural resonances and shears gear teeth. Modern Physical AI resolves this fundamental throughput mismatch through Action Chunking—generating multi-step future horizons that amortize computational latency, blended across time through receding-horizon ensembling and smoothed via $\mathcal{C}^2$ quintic splines to respect the physical limits of mass and mechanisms.

3. **Amortize Delay via Receding-Horizon Temporal Ensembling:** Formulate exponential ensemble blending ($w_i \propto e^{-k(t - t_i)}$) across overlapping prediction horizons, suppressing high-frequency diffusion sampling noise and eliminating boundary discontinuities.
4. **Enforce $\mathcal{C}^2$ Quintic Spline Continuity:** Formulate polynomial trajectory interpolation matching boundary position, velocity, and acceleration to strictly bound joint jerk ($\|\dddot{q}\| \le j_{\text{max}}$), protecting cycloidal reducers and harmonic drives from tooth shear [@murray2017mathematical].
5. **Architect the Action Chunking Interface:** Formalize the multi-step trajectory chunk specification between the Linux MPU and the real-time MCU.

**Core Chapter Takeaway:** Discrete neural steps starve actuators and excite destructive mechanical resonances; action chunking amortizes inference latency across time while continuous polynomial splines enforce the jerk limits required to protect physical gearboxes.

## Trajectory Planning in the Loop: Bridging Deliberation and Real-Time Control

To understand the role of trajectory generation within embodied artificial intelligence, we must locate this subsystem within the broader cognitive pipeline, as illustrated in @fig-locator-ch07. Trajectory planning operates as the critical translation layer bridging the slow semantic cognition of the host processor and the high-frequency motor reflex loops executed on bare-metal silicon. Downstream of semantic reasoning, the planner receives abstract, expiring intent leases denoted by $\mathcal{L}_{\text{intent}}$. These leases encode the desired target pose or task objective generated at a sparse cadence of one to two Hertz. 

The trajectory planner is responsible for unwrapping this semantic intent into a dense, physically realizable continuum of motion. By operating as a System 1.5 proposal engine, it emits continuous multi-step action chunks that map out the immediate future. This dense stream of target waypoints, denoted as $p_t$, feeds directly into the downstream real-time reflex enforcer. The reflex stage then evaluates safety constraints and computes the final high-frequency motor control effort $u_t^*$. Without this intermediate chunking stage, the high-frequency reflex controllers would be left waiting on slow semantic neural networks, resulting in disjointed and mechanically destructive behavior.

## Delay Amortization, Multimodality, and Mechanical Dynamics

When roboticists first attempted to connect deep neural policies directly to physical motors, they overwhelmingly adopted single-step Markovian architectures. In this naive formulation, a neural network ingests an observation and outputs a single commanded waypoint for the next time step. Because neural inference demands heavy matrix multiplication, the computation time $T_{\text{infer}}$ typically spans 20 to 50 milliseconds. Driving a high-frequency control loop with a sensorimotor latency of 50 milliseconds introduces a massive phase lag into the feedback system. The motor controller, starved of fresh commands while the network computes, holds the previous setpoint, resulting in control loops that oscillate wildly and ultimately succumb to tracking instability.

Beyond latency, deterministic single-step regression architectures fail to model the inherent multimodality of physical tasks. When minimizing a standard Mean Squared Error (MSE) loss function, a deterministic policy forced to choose between routing an end-effector to the left or the right of an obstacle will mathematically split the difference. Averaging two perfectly valid, disjoint trajectories yields a non-viable intermediate path, commanding the robot directly into the obstacle. True embodied policies must therefore model probability distributions over future states rather than regressing to a single mean prediction.

Furthermore, discrete trajectory updates generated across multi-millisecond intervals wreak havoc on mechanical transmissions. A step change in a velocity or position command produces an infinite derivative impulse. Because physical acceleration is the second time-derivative of position, instantaneous waypoint changes command infinite joint acceleration and infinite mechanical jerk ($\dddot{\mathbf{q}} \to \infty$). These discontinuous steps propagate down the kinematic chain, inducing severe torque ripple evaluated as $\dot{\boldsymbol{\tau}} = \mathbf{J}^T \mathbf{M} \dddot{\mathbf{q}}$. Unmitigated torque ripple fatigues harmonic drive flexsplines and regularly shears the rigid pins of cycloidal gearboxes, turning software latency directly into hardware destruction.

This dynamic reality manifests uniquely across the three canonical archetypes of Physical AI. In mobility applications, planners chunk continuous curvature profiles to prevent sudden lateral accelerations from rolling the chassis. In contact manipulation, robots generate multi-axis force profile chunks, predicting the compliance necessary to insert pegs or mate surfaces without shattering them. In cybernetic process control, agents emit predictive switching schedules, anticipating thermal lag and fluid momentum to maintain equilibrium. Across all archetypes, chunking amortizes latency and enforces the continuity required by the laws of physics.

## Silicon Ingestion and the AI Engine: ACT and Diffusion Policies

Modern generative action decoders depart from single-step regression, predicting continuous multi-step horizons in a single parallel inference pass. Two architectures dominate this space: Action Chunking Transformers (ACT) and Conditional Diffusion Policies.

The Action Chunking Transformer architecture frames trajectory generation as a conditional Sequence-to-Sequence task utilizing a Conditional Variational Autoencoder (CVAE). To overcome multimodal regression averaging, an encoder maps demonstration trajectories into a latent style variable parameterized as $z \sim \mathcal{N}(\boldsymbol{\mu}, \boldsymbol{\Sigma})$. During deployment, a transformer decoder ingests the sampled latent variable $z$ alongside visual observation tokens and proprioceptive state embeddings. The decoder utilizes cross-attention to output a fully unrolled $H$-step action chunk $\mathbf{A}_{t:t+H} = [\mathbf{q}_t, \mathbf{q}_{t+1}, \dots, \mathbf{q}_{t+H}]$ simultaneously, perfectly capturing the multimodal intent while bounding latency to a single network pass.

Diffusion Policies tackle multimodality through iterative denoising score matching. During training, a forward process injects Gaussian noise into demonstration trajectories according to $q(\mathbf{A}^k | \mathbf{A}^{k-1})$. At inference time, the network begins with pure Gaussian noise and iteratively subtracts predicted noise over a series of steps. This reverse denoising process utilizes 1D Temporal U-Nets conditioned heavily on observation tokens $O_t$. To achieve real-time performance, accelerated sampling algorithms like DDIM converge on a smooth trajectory chunk in as few as $K=4\text{--}8$ denoising steps.

Regardless of the generative engine, outputting discrete neural waypoints is insufficient for mechanical safety. Trajectories must be smoothed using $\mathcal{C}^2$ Quintic Polynomial Splines. By formulating a closed-form parameterization $s(\tau) = a_0 + a_1\tau + a_2\tau^2 + a_3\tau^3 + a_4\tau^4 + a_5\tau^5$, the system matches position, velocity, and acceleration boundary conditions precisely at both ends of the chunk. This high-order spline provides a mathematical guarantee that the maximum mechanical jerk is strictly bounded ($\|\dddot{\mathbf{q}}\| \le j_{\text{max}}$), eliminating the torque transients that cause fatigue and shear.

Finally, because neural networks process streams of video and proprioception asynchronously, inference jitter is unavoidable. To ensure smooth execution, Physical AI systems employ Receding-Horizon Temporal Ensembling. As new action chunks arrive from the policy, they overlap with previously generated chunks for the same physical time step. By blending these overlapping action chunks using exponential temporal weights proportional to $w_i \propto e^{-k(t - t_i)}$, the system effectively acts as a low-pass filter on generative variance. This ensembling continuously updates the commanded trajectory based on the freshest sensory data while entirely eliminating the discontinuous boundaries between successive network predictions.

## Forensic Systems Failure Anatomy: The Sheared Cycloidal Drive Pin

::: {.callout-autopsy title="The Sheared Cycloidal Drive Pin"}
**Platform:** Precision Articulated Bimanual Manipulator ($20\text{ Hz}$ Diffusion Policy).
**Failure Mechanism:** Executing sequential action chunks without temporal ensembling or $\mathcal{C}^2$ quintic spline interpolation allowed an unmitigated velocity step between consecutive chunks ($\Delta \dot{q} = 1.07\text{ rad/s}$ across $1\text{ ms}$).
**Root Cause:** Instantaneous acceleration spike ($\ddot{q} = 1{,}070\text{ rad/s}^2$) generated a $48.2\text{ N}\cdot\text{m}$ dynamic torque shock exceeding the cycloidal reducer shear limit ($28.0\text{ N}\cdot\text{m}$).
**Physical Consequence:** Planetary drive pins sheared instantly, detaching the joint 2 linkage and dropping a $12\text{ kg}$ fixture payload onto the workbench ($3,800\text{ USD}$ overhaul).
:::

![The Precision Articulated Bimanual Manipulator. An unmitigated velocity step between consecutive chunks generated an instantaneous acceleration of $1{,}070\text{ rad/s}^2$, producing a $48.2\text{ N}\cdot\text{m}$ torque pulse that sheared the cycloidal reducer planetary drive pins.](figures/fig07_manipulator_arm_cropped.jpg){#fig-planning-platform width=100%}

In the autopsy referenced above, a high-payload articulated manipulator was driven by a diffusion policy emitting sequential action chunks. The software architecture dispatched these discrete neural waypoints directly to the motor inverter arrays without applying receding-horizon temporal ensembling or quintic spline interpolation. During a downward sweeping motion, Joint 2 reached a chunk boundary and was instantly commanded from a velocity of $-0.42\text{ rad/s}$ to $+0.65\text{ rad/s}$. Because the motor controller operated on a one millisecond tick, this velocity discontinuity commanded an acceleration spike of $\ddot{q}_2 = 1{,}070\text{ rad/s}^2$. 

The inertia of the linkage demanded a dynamic torque pulse of $48.2\text{ N}\cdot\text{m}$ to satisfy this sudden acceleration constraint. This massive, instantaneous demand vastly exceeded the $28.0\text{ N}\cdot\text{m}$ shear threshold of the cycloidal reducer's hardened steel planetary pins. The pins sheared completely, mechanically detaching the arm and dropping the heavy payload. @tbl-telemetry-ch07 reconstructs the microsecond-level telemetry sequence, revealing how a seemingly benign software discontinuity propagated through the motor inverter to cause catastrophic mechanical failure.

| Timestamp | Subsystem & Substrate | Recorded State / Telemetry Event | Physical Implication |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **$T + 21.430\text{ s}$** | Linux MPU / Diffusion Model | Evaluates Chunk $k$; joint 2 sweeping downward ($\dot{q}_2 = -0.42\text{ rad/s}$). | Nominal descent trajectory active. |
| **$T + 21.450\text{ s}$** | Policy Ingestion / SRAM Mailbox | Chunk $k+1$ arrives; initial waypoint commands reversal ($\dot{q}_2 = +0.65\text{ rad/s}$). | $\Delta \dot{q} = 1.07\text{ rad/s}$ velocity discontinuity. |
| **$T + 21.451\text{ s}$** | Joint 2 Inverter Controller | Single-tick velocity step applied without spline smoothing ($\Delta t = 1\text{ ms}$). | Commanded acceleration spikes to $\ddot{q} = 1{,}070\text{ rad/s}^2$. |
| **$T + 21.452\text{ s}$** | Joint 2 Motor Stator | Phase current surges to $28.5\text{ A}$; motor outputs $48.2\text{ N}\cdot\text{m}$ torque shock. | Torque pulse exceeds shear threshold ($28.0\text{ N}\cdot\text{m}$). |
| **$T + 21.453\text{ s}$** | Cycloidal Reducer Gearbox | Hardened steel planetary drive pins shear through under $4.2\text{ kN}$ pin force. | Mechanical disconnect; payload drops ($3,800\text{ USD}$ overhaul). |
| **Root Cause** | *Systems Bottleneck* | Chunk-to-chunk boundary velocity discontinuity dispatched directly to motor drives. | Spline smoothing omitted. |
| **Architectural Flaw** | *Privilege & Co-Design* | Lack of receding-horizon temporal ensembling and hardware torque-rate limits. | Controller lacked $\|\dot{\boldsymbol{\tau}}\| \le \dot{\tau}_{\text{max}}$. |

## The Trajectory Chunk Interface Specification and Co-Design Checkpoint

To formalize the handoff between the Linux-hosted generative planners and the bare-metal microcontrollers, systems architects define a strict Trajectory Chunk Interface. This specification ensures that the output vector $p_t = [\mathbf{q}_1, \dots, \mathbf{q}_H]$ is structurally sound, predictable, and within the dynamic limits of the actuation hardware before it ever reaches the motor drives.

| Parameter Category | Specification Key | Engineering Target Value | Verification Boundary |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Chunk Horizon** | `chunk.horizon_steps_H` | $16\text{ steps}$ | $800\text{ ms}$ forward prediction reservoir |
| **Step Interval** | `chunk.step_interval_ms` | $50.0\text{ ms}$ ($20\text{ Hz}$) | Constant discretization cadence |
| **Ensemble Overlap** | `ensemble.overlap_window` | $8\text{ steps}$ ($400\text{ ms}$) | Multi-horizon blending window |
| **Ensemble Decay Rate** | `ensemble.lambda_weight` | $0.25$ ($w_i = e^{-0.25 i}$) | Temporal exponential weighting |
| **Max Joint Jerk** | `spline.max_joint_jerk_rad_s3` | $25.0\text{ rad/s}^3$ | $\mathcal{C}^2$ quintic spline bound |
| **Max Torque Rate** | `actuator.max_torque_rate_nm_s` | $150.0\text{ N}\cdot\text{m/s}$ | Prevents mechanical gear tooth shock |
| **Queue Depth** | `mailbox.shared_sram_slots` | $2\text{ slots}$ (Double buffer) | Zero-copy lock-free ring buffer |

: The Trajectory Planning Specification. Chunk horizons, temporal ensembling parameters, and derivative continuity bounds bridging Planning to Execution. {#tbl-planning-spec}

This rigorous definition of the planning interface is further scrutinized through a comprehensive 5-Column Matrix Checkpoint audit. By explicitly tracing each high-level software constraint back to its root physical cause, the matrix enforces an architectural resolution that guarantees safe mechanical execution.

| Constraint Category | Subsystem Tension | Root Physical Cause | Architectural Resolution | Validation Boundary |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Time & Freshness** | Neural forward latency ($20\text{--}50\text{ ms}$) starves 1 kHz loops. | Silicon throughput bottleneck. | **Action Chunking ($H=16$)** amortizing compute across time. | Mailbox underflow rate $\le 0.1\%$ |
| **Inertia & Stopping** | Multi-step plans command obsolete motions upon obstacles. | Momentum cannot be frozen. | Receding-horizon replanning ($20\text{ Hz}$) and MCU safety vetoes. | Collision voidance latency $\le 2\text{ ms}$ |
| **Actuation & Jerk** | Discrete neural waypoints command infinite acceleration. | Step-functions have infinite derivatives. | **$\mathcal{C}^2$ Quintic Polynomial Splines** bounding jerk ($\dddot{\mathbf{q}} \le j_{\text{max}}$). | Accelerometer vibration spectra |
| **Energy & Thermal** | Rapid motor reversals draw massive $I^2R$ peak currents. | Unconstrained $\Delta V$ across motor coils. | Torque-rate limiting ($\dot{\boldsymbol{\tau}} \le \dot{\tau}_{\text{max}}$) smoothing power draw. | Peak current draw logs |
| **Silicon Determinism** | Stochastic diffusion sampling noise introduces path jitter. | Generative variance over sequential runs. | **Receding-Horizon Temporal Ensembling** in shared SRAM. | Tool center point path deviation |

## Chapter Summary and Forward Handoff

This chapter has established the necessity and the mechanics of trajectory action chunking as a critical bridge between cognitive inference and mechanical reality. We diagnosed the profound instability caused by single-step Markovian delay and demonstrated how generative decoders—like ACT and Diffusion Policies—amortize this latency by producing broad prediction horizons. Through receding-horizon temporal ensembling and $\mathcal{C}^2$ quintic polynomial splines, these discrete neural predictions are mathematically transformed into continuous, jerk-bounded trajectories that safely drive high-frequency motor inverters without shearing gearbox pins.

With the trajectory securely chunked, smoothed, and deposited into the shared SRAM mailboxes, the baton passes to the lowest level of the physical stack. In the following chapter, **Chapter 8 (Execute: Deterministic 1 kHz Reflexes and Control Barrier Functions)**, we dive into the bare-metal microcontroller silicon. We will explore how real-time execution engines ingest these polynomial splines, calculate inverse kinematics at one kilohertz, and evaluate rigid non-negotiable safety invariants before finally committing current to the motor stator coils.
